classification.difficultyReason: Uses the explicitly requested quadratic formula for roots, calculates the vertex and y-intercept, then combines these features with concavity in a sketch.

content.prompt: Using the quadratic formula, find the $x$-intercepts of each of the following parabolas and then sketch their graphs. Label the coordinates of the turning point and the axial intercepts.

answer.worked:
At $x=0$, $y=-4$. For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{2^2-4(1)(-4)}}{2(1)}\\x&=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{20}}2\\x&=-1\pm\sqrt5.\end{align*}$$
The turning point is at
$$\begin{align*}x&=-\frac{2}{2(1)}=-1,\\y&=(-1)^2+2(-1)-4=-5.\end{align*}$$
The axis of symmetry is $x=-1$. The positive coefficient of $x^2$ gives an upward-opening parabola.

spec.description: Complete solution sketch with black axes, curve and four labelled feature points; no grid or numeric ticks.

$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{2^2-4(-1)(2)}}{2(-1)}\\x&=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{12}}{-2}\\x&=1\pm\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$
